title: Generic descent of the square difference over a normal integral base
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$ be its generic point, whose residue field $k(S)$ is its function field [def-sc-generic-point, def-sc-function-field]. For $i=1,2,3$, let $X_i\to S$ be smooth separated morphisms of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with geometrically integral fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: for each $s\in S$, the fibre over its residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is integral after every extension of $\kappa(s)$. In particular all fibres are nonempty. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Put $C=X_1\times_SX_2\times_SX_3$, $P=X_1\times_SX_1\times_SX_2\times_SX_2$, and $\pi:P\times_SX_3\to P$. At coordinates $(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1,z)$ write $r_{ab}(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1,z)=(x_a,y_b,z)$ for $a,b\in\{0,1\}$. For an invertible module $A$ on $C$, define its square difference by $$D(A)=r_{00}^*A\otimes r_{11}^*A\otimes(r_{01}^*A)^{-1}\otimes(r_{10}^*A)^{-1}.$$ Here inverse means the dual invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], and all products, pullbacks and tensors are those of [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If there is an invertible $N_\eta$ on $P_\eta=P\times_S\eta$ with $$D(A)|_{(P\times_SX_3)_\eta}\cong\pi_\eta^*N_\eta,$$ then there is an invertible module $N$ on $P$ with $$D(A)\cong\pi^*N.$$

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.2(i), specialized to smooth separated finite-presentation factors with geometrically integral fibres; March 31, 2026 author version, printed pp.11-12, read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Form successively $B_0=S$, $B_1=X_1$, $B_2=X_1\times_SX_1$, $B_3=B_2\times_SX_2$, and $B_4=B_3\times_SX_2=P$. Each projection $B_j\to B_{j-1}$ is the base change of one of the given smooth maps, hence smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. For $b\in B_{j-1}$ with image $s\in S$, its fibre is $X_{i,s}\times_{\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$. After any field extension of $\kappa(b)$ it is still a field extension of $X_{i,s}$, so it is integral and nonempty by the hypothesis; in particular it is geometrically connected. Starting with normal integral $B_0$, apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] at each projection to conclude that every $B_j$ is normal and integral. Nonemptiness holds at each stage because all its fibres over the nonempty previous stage are nonempty. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] the projections are locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type (a finite presentation has finitely many generators). Starting with locally Noetherian $S$, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] at each projection makes every $B_j$ locally Noetherian. Thus $P$ is normal integral locally Noetherian. Every projection is surjective by its nonempty fibres, so $P\to S$ is surjective.

source.place: Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth) and 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); normal integral total spaces as in the cited geometry-core statement (034F, 056T, 01UA).

proof.text: Put $Y=P\times_SX_3$ and $M=D(A)$. The projection $\pi:Y\to P$ is smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and therefore flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. In particular it is locally of finite type. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] with the locally Noetherian base $P$ to obtain locally Noetherian $Y$. For every $p\in P$ over $s\in S$, the fibre $Y_p$ is $X_{3,s}\times_{\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)$, hence integral and nonempty by geometric integrality in the hypothesis. These are precisely the residue-field fibres of $\pi$, not just its fibres over points of $S$.

source.place: Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); verification of hypotheses (1)--(4) of divisors.tex Tag 0BD7 (lemma-in-image-pullback).

proof.text: Let $\xi=\operatorname{Spec}k(P)$ be the generic point of the integral scheme $P$. Its image in $S$ is $\eta$: every point of $P$ is a specialization of $\xi$, so surjectivity of $P\to S$ implies that every point of $S$ is a specialization of its image; an integral scheme has only one generic point. The map $\xi\to P$ therefore factors through $P_\eta$; write this map as $j:\xi\to P_\eta$. Pull back the assumed isomorphism along $Y_\xi\to Y_\eta$. Functoriality of tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the fibre-product identities give $M|_{Y_\xi}\cong\pi_\xi^*(j^*N_\eta)$. By the rank-one local-frame definition [def-sc-invertible-module], $j^*N_\eta$ is a one-dimensional vector space over $k(P)$; choosing a nonzero basis gives $j^*N_\eta\cong\mathcal O_\xi$, hence $M|_{Y_\xi}\cong\mathcal O_{Y_\xi}$. Also $M$ is invertible: near each point of $Y$, pull back local frames for the four factors of $D(A)$ and tensor them, using the dual frames for the two inverse factors. These frames locally identify $M$ with $\mathcal O_Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7 (lemma-in-image-pullback), hypothesis (5); elementary generic-point reduction, as in Guo Proposition 5.2(i), printed p.11.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] to $f=\pi:Y\to P$ and $M=D(A)$. Its normal integral locally Noetherian base hypothesis is step 1; its locally Noetherian source, flatness, integral nonempty fibres and locally-of-finite-type alternative are step 2; its invertibility and generic-fibre triviality hypotheses are step 3. It yields an invertible $\mathcal O_P$-module $N$ with $\pi^*N\cong D(A)$. Inverting this isomorphism gives the required $D(A)\cong\pi^*N$.
